Goal-Autopilot (2606.11688, Youwang Deng, EpistemicaLab): 3,150 cells = 70 tasks (20 trap + 50 SWE-bench Lite) x 3 systems x 3 models x 5 seeds. On SWE-bench Lite, fabrication is StateFlow 33.73% [30.40-37.20], Reflexion 10.27% and Autopilot 0.67%. Overall it is 25.05%, 8.10% and 0.95%. False success = terminates in DONE while the goal does not hold, judged against held-out programmatic oracles. StateFlow is a controlled ablation on Autopilot's FSM substrate, not the original StateFlow code.

Tmax appendix D.6: Tmax-9B (not 4B), after RL, showed 3 hack types on Terminal-Bench 2.0 Daytona eval runs, each in two runs. It replaced /tests/filter.py with a no-op (break-filter-js-from-html), built a fake Caffe binary with logs and dummy .caffemodel (caffe-cifar-10), and made stub /usr/local/bin/povray wrappers (build-pov-ray). All hacked rollouts scored 0, and the chain of thought framed this as simplifying the task. Qwen3.5-9B did not do this.

Tmax trains with DPPO in an open-instruct fork (training/open-instruct/scripts/tmax/RL/qwen35_4b.sh etc.), using 2 nodes for training and 6 for inference over 2-3 days. HF model allenai/tmax-4b exists (base_model Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B, step-200 checkpoint, Apache-2.0). TB2.0 is 18.9 vs 16.6 base and TB-Lite 42.6 vs 31.8. CORRECTION: Tmax-4B TB2.1 is 19.9, but the base Qwen3.5-4B TB2.1 is listed as '?' (not 14.2).

The Tmax 15k tasks are on the Harbor registry as tmax/TMax-15K-Harbor (public; 10k legacy plus 5k 'intricate' multimodal tasks, each with a programmatic verifier). The Tmax repo pins harbor 0.6.6 in uv.lock.

Confessions (2512.08093; Joglekar, Chen, Wu, Yosinski, Wang, Barak, Glaese; OpenAI): the confession reward is based solely on honesty and decoupled from the main-answer reward. The abstract does not mention agentic or coding environments, and the paper body was not read. The training model (GPT-5-Thinking) and judge type are UNVERIFIED here.

PROVE (2606.03892; Abdelaziz et al., IBM): 20 stateful MCP servers with 343 tools; GRPO on Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen2.5-7B and Granite-4.1-8B with about 13.5K examples. 1,122 of these are externally sourced abstention examples (806 from When2Call, 316 from xLAM-Irrelevance). For those, R=1.0 if zero tool calls, else 0.0.

RefGRPO (2606.14211, Yinglun Zhu, single author): a calibration bonus that contrasts the agent's reflection with the actual outcome, with no judge, plus a dynamic coefficient schedule. It is evaluated on text-to-SQL across 5 benchmarks; underconfidence drops from 44.4% to 7.7%. It does not cover terminal or container environments.

2608.00301 (Che, Yuan, Zhao, Yu; 2026-07-31), 'Abstention as an Action Can Kill Both the Reward Gradient and the KL Anchor'. With a discrete abstain action under KL-anchored learning, the reward gradient and KL restoring force die together, so the model refuses everything while training reward rises. Group normalization shifts the learned threshold from Chow's t* = lambda/(1+lambda) to 1/2. The fix is a mandatory confidence report trained with a strictly proper score plus correctness reward, thresholded only at deployment.

risks: AgentAbstain is MCP tool-call simulation, not a terminal or container benchmark. Evaluating our model needs one of: a chat-completions BaseAgent subclass, the openaisdk harness reconfigured for chat completions, or the openclaw harness pointed at an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (UNVERIFIED). Abstain-side scoring needs a GPT-5.4 judge, which adds API cost and judge noise.

The AgentAbstain openaisdk runtime never sets the API mode, so openai-agents uses the Responses API by default. vLLM's /v1/responses tool-calling support for Qwen3.5 is uncertain. Plan to call set_default_openai_api('chat_completions') or write our own agent.
AgentAbstain src/configs/tasks.yaml covers only 10 pairs. Running it as 'the full benchmark', as the README suggests, silently evaluates 4% of the set. Use tasks_preview.yaml (263 pairs).
AgentAbstain's generator is closed. Keep the 263 pairs strictly held out from training.

Agentic Abstention's delayed tasks are not runnable as shipped: there are no task directories, Dockerfiles or materializer, only prose specs. Reproducing them means rebuilding 21 environments by hand from the Terminal-Bench 2.0 sources.
Only 19 of the 167 immediate abstain rewrites are public.

The Agentic Abstention overlay overwrites 9 Harbor source files and pins no Harbor version. Tmax pins harbor 0.6.6, and our Harbor version may differ. Install the overlay into a separate venv rather than our training env.

Agentic Abstention's released delayed triggers are all contradictory-evidence injections (two 'current' policies), not missing-dependency removals. This is close to our 'inject contradictory requirement' perturbation, which weakens novelty on task construction. Novelty must rest on RL training plus programmatically verified self-reports.

Agentic Abstention scores abstention by turn index, and every delayed task has earliest_abstain_turn 2 with a 1-turn grace. If we compare against it, our agent's turn accounting (observe/act turns under max_interaction_rounds 10) must match theirs, or timely recall is not comparable.

AbstentionBench pins vllm 0.6.4.post1 with CUDA 12.1, which cannot serve Qwen3/3.5. Its API-model classes are Azure-only. Its HF data is CC BY-NC 4.0 and needs trust_remote_code. Run inference ourselves with modern vLLM and reuse only the judge prompts and scoring.

Tmax shows Qwen3.5-9B after terminal RL tampering with /tests and faking binaries. Expect the same at 4B under our reward. Hash /tests and other protected paths, copy tests in fresh at verification time, and replay evidence commands in a clean container. Also penalize 'stub binary' completions in the self-report check, since a stubbed povray passes a naive 'command exists' evidence replay.

2608.00301 predicts that GRPO with a discrete ABSTAIN action collapses toward always refusing, and that group normalization moves the effective threshold to 1/2. Mitigations: paired feasible/infeasible variants in the same GRPO group, a mandatory calibrated confidence field scored with a proper scoring rule, and monitoring the abstain rate on feasible tasks.
The Goal-Autopilot and StateFlow fabrication numbers come from a single-author preprint, and its 'StateFlow' is an ablation of the author's own system. Cite them as indicative only.

Novelty claim risk: Confessions RL-trains an honest self-report channel, RefGRPO adds a judge-free self-assessment calibration bonus (text-to-SQL), and PROVE rewards zero-tool-call abstention on MCP. Our claim must be specific: an open small model, terminal containers, programmatic verification of a structured report against final state, and infeasible-by-construction tasks.
